SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

MAY 29 1939

Bluff, Not Legality
THE Shanghai Municipal Council has for months been fighting a rearguard action against Japanese encroachments north of the Soochow Creek as we all know. At times there have been some advances in the direction of recovering a measure of Council jurisdiction, or at least responsibility, in those parts of the Settlement lying within the "Japanese defense sector". But upon the whole it must be confessed that the situation for the past nineteen months or so has remained discouraging-to-alarming.
Developments of the past few days do not necessarily heighten the alarming features of the case but they certainly put on record an increased amount of information showing how the Japanese notion of a virtual Japanese Concession within Settlement boundaries has spread and hardened.
Summed up, the position is that in the words of the official spokesmen, the Japanese regard all areas north of Soochow Creek as being "under Japanese military occupation"—a state of affairs warranting them, in their own estimation, in proceeding with any such matters as the recent promulgation of special traffic regulations quite independent of the ones already enforced by the Shanghai Municipal Council in all parts of the Settlement where effective control is maintained.
It appears that the Japanese feel themselves justified in this virtual seizure of a considerable part of the Settlement because in the early days of the fighting, the Chinese army for short periods entered and held small sections of the Settlement territory. It does not seem that the Japanese wish to stand firmly on a point of rights under international law in this connection, but their view would appear to be that they do not find the situation to be outside the scope of international law. In other words, maybe international law just doesn't cover the case!

1939年5月29日

虚张声势，而非依法行事

众所周知，上海公共租界工部局数月来一直在苏州河以北地区对日本的蚕食行动进行后卫战。有时，在收回位于“日本防区”内的租界部分区域的工部局管辖权，或至少是责任方面，取得了一些进展。但总体而言，必须承认，过去十九个月左右的局势一直令人沮丧，甚至令人担忧。

过去几天的事态发展未必加剧了本案的令人担忧之处，但它们确实记录在案了大量信息，显示日本关于在租界边界内建立事实上的日本专管租界的观念是如何扩散和固化的。

概括来说，正如官方发言人所言，目前的局势是：日本方面将苏州河以北的所有区域视为“处于日本军事占领之下”——这种状态在他们自己看来，足以证明其有权推行诸如最近颁布的特别交通法规等事项，而这些法规完全独立于上海公共租界工部局在所有维持有效控制区域的现行法规。

看来，日本方面认为自己有理由事实上夺取租界相当大的一部分，因为在战斗初期，中国军队曾短暂进入并控制了租界领土的小部分区域。日本方面似乎并不希望在此问题上 firmly 坚持国际法下的权利立场，但他们的观点似乎是，他们认为这种情况并不超出国际法的范围。换句话说，也许国际法根本就不涵盖此案！

war was declared, nor has any been declared
yet. In 1932, with roughly comparable circum-

a partnership which—as the Japanese were
themselves fighting the Chinese—was most
galling to the other armed forces and to the
Council. So in 1937 the Council avoided in-
voking this formal condition of defense
partnership. Therefore the Japanese had no
such link with the other forces which quietly
assumed their various assigned defense sectors

since held them, but with nothing like the
arrogation of traffic-control and other func-
tions which the Japanese have taken over
without permission from anybody.
In the first place, there is no formalized
state of war. And in the second place, the
obviously existing hostilities are not directed
against the International Settlement. There-
fore it is most difficult to fathom on what
juridical basis the Japanese could lay claim to
any right to control traffic or to seize and
utilize foreign, or even Chinese, properties. The
situation seems simply to be one of force
majeure. What the Japanese armed forces
have, they hold, no matter to whom it may
happen to belong. That appears the net of it.

MAR 24 1939
MUNICIPAL 68
S. B: REGISTRY
No. S. L. D.
Date

Gratifying to Shanghailanders was the action of the Council's own demarche department in protesting the Japanese Naval Police Party's amendments and additions to the existing traffic regulations. At one time it was thought that the Council would have to appeal, but the S.M.C. informed the Nipponese authorities that traffic regulations, even in Hongkew and Yangtszepoo, could be altered only by the Shanghai Municipal Police.

Reports that Chinese, arrested in the International Settlement by the S.M.P. upon request of the Japanese authorities, have been handed over north of the creek are untrue.
From unimpeachable sources, we learned that up to 4 p.m. yesterday, none of the Chinese arrested was turned over to the Nipponese authorities.
No assurances could be given that such arrests would not be handed over in the future, however.

Incidentally, the recent accord reached between the Shanghai Municipal Council and the Japanese is said to provide lessening provocation.

One case reported yesterday was that a Chinese was arrested in the Yangtze Hotel recently simply because an acquaintance of his, who bore him personal malice, wrote to the Japanese Special Service Section stating that the object of his dislike was a guerilla.
If it becomes as easy as that to put one's acquaintances into soup or boiling oil, perhaps this city is not going to be much of a place to live in.

It is now apparent that many years will pass before foreign guests will take accommodation in the Astor House again. Contrary to previous reports, it is now learned that the 40-year-old hostelry has been leased to a private operator for five years. The lease, which expires in January 1944, contains a lessee's option to renew after the date of expiration.

工部局自身的交涉部门抗议日本海军警察队对现有交通法规的修订和增补，这一行动令上海外籍居民感到欣慰。曾有一度认为工部局不得不提出上诉，但工部局告知日本方面，即使在虹口和杨树浦，交通法规也只能由上海公共租界警务处更改。

顺便提一下，据说上海公共租界工部局与日本最近达成的协议旨在减少挑衅。

工部局抗议
交通法规

继日本特别海军陆战队发布一套 lengthy 的交通法规以管理上海海军防区内的车辆交通后，上海公共租界工部局于昨日向日本当局提出抗议。

虽然抗议书的官方文本未予公开，但《字林西报》获悉，该照会指出，发布此类法规是上海公共租界工部局的职能，而非日本特别海军陆战队的职能，因为该防区位于国际租界范围内。

新法规于昨日公布，并于3月15日生效。法规从第1条至第58条，最后以“凡违反本条例者，视情节禁止在日本特别海军陆战队管辖区域内驾驶车辆”结尾。工部局抗议书的副本已递交给领事团。

MAR 23 1939

Japanese Traffic Rules
The Shanghai Municipal Council has quite correctly protested to the Japanese authorities regarding the new traffic regulations devised for operation "on roads lying within the limits under the jurisdiction of the Japanese Naval Landing Party in Shanghai." The text of these regulations was published in this journal yesterday. The Council's attitude in the matter is perfectly correct. As the area claimed to be within the limits of Japanese jurisdiction is an integral part of the International Settlement which is administered by the Council the proper authority for promulgating any form of traffic regulations is the Council. Although the area designated is claimed to be under Japanese control, it is a defence sector within the limits of the International Settlement. This point, in another way, was made by the Council in regard to the recent Japanese demands for the suppression of terrorism when it was stated that, without the sanction of all the Powers concerned, the Council has no power to delegate the police powers and responsibilities entrusted to it by the Land Regulations. Within this scope of police powers is the maintenance of traffic conduct in the Settlement and as the existing traffic regulations work efficiently enough judged by normal standards there is no necessity on the part of the Japanese for modification or elaboration. An examination of the regulations shows a number of inconsistencies and the final article holds a threat, which it is hoped, will not be carried out." Whoever violates these regulations will be prohibited to drive a vehicle in the areas under the jurisdiction of the Shanghai Special Naval Landing Party according to the circumstances," this article reads. In other words, there is a complete disregard of the regulations already in existence and an assumption of the authority vested in the Shanghai Municipal Council.

日本交通法规
上海公共租界工部局就日本当局为“在上海日本海军陆战队管辖范围内的道路”实施的新交通法规，向日方提出了完全正确的抗议。这些法规的文本已于昨日在本刊刊登。工部局在此事上的立场完全正确。由于被声称属于日本管辖范围的区域是国际公共租界不可分割的一部分，而该租界由工部局管理，因此颁布任何形式的交通法规的适当权力机构是工部局。尽管指定区域被声称处于日本控制之下，但它仍是国际公共租界界限内的一个防务区。关于这一点，工部局在回应日本近期提出的镇压恐怖主义要求时，曾以另一种方式指出：未经所有相关列强批准，工部局无权将《土地章程》赋予它的警察权力和责任委托给他人。维持租界内的交通秩序属于这一警察权力范围，而且鉴于现行交通法规按照正常标准判断已足够有效运作，日方并无必要进行修改或细化。审查这些法规会发现其中存在多处不一致之处，且最后一条款带有威胁意味，希望该威胁不会付诸实施。“凡违反本规定者，视情节轻重，禁止在上海特别海军陆战队管辖区域内驾驶车辆，”该条款如此写道。换言之，这是对既有的法规完全无视，并僭越了归属于上海公共租界工部局的权力。

MAR 22 1939
Japanese Traffic Rules
Regulations Governing Vehicular Movements in
Areas Controlled by Naval Landing Party

THE following traffic regulations concerning motor vehicular
traffic naval sector were promulgated on February 20 and
were to have come into force on March 15. Non-parking areas,
speed limits, waiting sections, licences and methods of passing
vehicles are outlined. It will be noted that the Japanese recognize
licences issued by the "Ta Tao" government.

Article 1. These regulations are to
be applied to motor vehicular traffic
on roads lying within the limits under
the jurisdiction of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party in Shanghai.
Article 2. In these regulations any
vehicle which is driven by a motor
and does not run on tracks shall be
designated as a motor vehicle.
Article 3. In these regulations the
section of highway intended for the
use of vehicles shall be defined as a
roadway and the section intended for
the use of pedestrians shall be called
a footpath. Generally the footpaths
on both sides of a highway have a
kerb; in case there is no kerb on a
highway one-sixth of the width on
both sides of the highway sall be re-
garded as footpaths and the rest as
a roadway.
Article 4. In these regulations any
portion of a roadway from which
vehicles are excluded shall be called
a Safety Zone.
Article 5. In these regulations a
path marked on a highway connecting
kerbs, indicating a crossing place for
pedestrians, shall be called Pedes-
trians Crossing.
Article 6. In these regulations the
term vehicle shall apply to all means
of transporting goods.
Article 7. In these regulations the
term Driver shall apply to any person
who, for the time being, is in charge
of a vehicle on a highway.
Article 8. In these regulations the
term passenger shall apply to any
occupant of a vehicle other than the
driver or a servant of the owner of
the vehicle actually in the perfor-
mance of his duty.
Article 9. In these regulations the
term pedestrian shall apply to any
person on foot on a highway. Pro-
vided that skaters, children's per-
ambulators and invalids' chairs shall
be considered as pedestrians when on
a footpath.
Article 10. In these regulations
the term waiting shall apply to any
vehicle standing on a highway for the
purpose of taking on or setting down
a person or persons or loading or
unloading things; and to a vehicle
waiting for a traffic signal or to avoid
an accident for the time being.
Furthermore, in these regulations the
term parking shall apply to a vehicle
standing on a highway other than
waiting. Provided that the vehicle
standing on a highway more than five
minutes while waiting shall be re-
garded as parking.
Article 11. In these regulations the
term Vehicle Stand shall apply to a
portion of a roadway or other space
specially set apart for the ranking or
parking of vehicles.
Article 12. No person shall drive
a vehicle on a highway in a
dangerous, reckless, negligent or
otherwise improper manner.
Article 13. No person shall drive
a vehicle on a highway, or stop at
any portion of a highway, in such a
manner as to cause unnecessary
obstruction to other traffic.
Article 14. No person shall board,
mount or enter or leave or descend
from a vehicle on a highway when
it is moving or in such a manner as
to cause unnecessary obstruction to
other traffic or when the vehicle is
drawn up alongside the curb.
Article 15. No person shall load or
unload cargo or goods on a highway
in such a manner as to cause unneces-
sary obstruction to traffic.

Article 16. No person shall carry
or place a load or any other article
on a highway in such a manner as to
cause unnecessary obstruction to
traffic. Necessary equipment should
be fitted to prevent the scattering or
leaking or dropping or any other.
Article 17. Every driver on a
highway shall promptly obey the
orders or signals of a sentry, gen-
darme or police (Consular Police,
"Reformed Government Police,"
specially the Shanghai Municipal
Police detailed for this purpose).
Article 18. No vehicle is permitted
to be driven at a speed of more than
30 km. an hour within the city limit
and 40 km. outside the city. The
vehicles of the Fire Brigade and
ambulances are excepted from these
regulations.
Article 19. No driver shall exceed
the speed stipulated in the preceding
Article, having due regard to the
rights of other users of the highway,
to existing traffic conditions, to the
state of the road surface, to the
presence of dangerous points,
(whether indicated or otherwise) and
to the danger of public.
Article 20. No vehicle shall be
permitted on a highway which is not
wide enough to allow two and a half
vehicles to pass each other. Provided
there is some space on the highway
where one vehicle can wait until the
other has passed ; such space must be
large enough to permit one and a
half vehicles to pass.

日本交通法规
管辖海军陆战队控制区域车辆通行的法规

以下关于机动车在海
军防区通行的交通法规于2月20日颁布，原定于3月15日生效。文中概述了禁停区、限速、等候区、执照及车辆通行方法。值得注意的是，日本人承认“大道”政府签发的执照。

第一条. 本法规适用于上海日本海军陆战队管辖范围内道路上的机动车交通。
第二条. 在本法规中，任何由马达驱动且不在轨道上行驶的车辆均 designated 为机动车。
第三条. 在本法规中，供车辆使用的公路部分定义为车道，供行人使用的部分称为人行道。通常公路两侧的人行道设有路缘石；若公路无路缘石，则公路两侧各六分之一的宽度视为人行道，其余部分视为车道。
第四条. 在本法规中，禁止车辆进入的任何车道部分称为安全区。
第五条. 在本法规中，公路上标记的连接路缘石、指示行人穿越处的路径称为人行横道。
第六条. 在本法规中，“车辆”一词适用于所有运输货物的手段。
第七条. 在本法规中，“驾驶员”一词适用于任何暂时在公路上负责车辆的人。
第八条. 在本法规中，“乘客”一词适用于除驾驶员或正在实际履行职责的车辆所有者仆役以外的任何车内乘员。
第九条. 在本法规中，“行人”一词适用于在公路上的任何步行者。但溜冰者、儿童推车及残疾人轮椅在人行道上时，应视为行人。
第十条. 在本法规中，“等候”一词适用于任何停在公路上以便上下人员或装卸物品的车辆；以及暂时等待交通信号或避免事故的车辆。此外，在本法规中，“停车”一词适用于除等候以外停在公路上的车辆。但等候时在公路上停留超过五分钟的车辆应视为停车。
第十一条. 在本法规中，“车辆停靠站”一词适用于专门划出供车辆排队或停放的车道部分或其他空间。
第十二条. 任何人不得以危险、鲁莽、疏忽或其他不当方式在公路上驾驶车辆。
第十三条. 任何人不得以对其他交通造成不必要阻碍的方式在公路上驾驶车辆，或在公路的任何部分停车。
第十四条. 任何人不得在车辆行驶时，或以对其他交通造成不必要阻碍的方式，或在车辆沿路缘石停靠时，在公路上登上、骑上、进入、离开或下车。
第十五条. 任何人不得以对交通造成不必要阻碍的方式在公路上装卸货物或物品。

第十六条. 任何人不得以对交通造成不必要阻碍的方式在公路上携带或放置负载或任何其他物品。应配备必要的设备以防止散落、泄漏、掉落或其他情况。
第十七条. 公路上的每位驾驶员应立即服从哨兵、宪兵或警察（领事警察、“维新政府”警察，特别是为此目的派遣的上海公共租界巡捕）的命令或信号。
第十八条. 任何车辆在市界内行驶速度不得超过每小时30公里，市界外不得超过每小时40公里。消防队和救护车的车辆不受本法规限制。
第十九条. 驾驶员在遵守前条规定的限速时，应适当顾及其他公路使用者的权利、现有交通状况、路面状况、危险点的存在（无论是否有标示）以及公众的危险。
第二十条. 任何公路若宽度不足以让两辆半车辆相互通过，则不允许车辆通行。但若公路上有空间可供一辆车等候直到另一辆车通过；则该空间必须足够大，以允许一辆半车辆通过。
第二十一条. 驾驶员应保持在车道的左侧行驶——速度越慢，越靠近路缘石。
第二十二条. 驾驶员不得向右穿越车道。
第二十三条. 驾驶员向左转弯时，应尽可能靠近左侧路缘石。
第二十四条. 驾驶员向右转弯时应大弧度转弯，并进入新车道中心线的左侧。交通繁忙时，驾驶员应避免穿越路口。
第二十五条. 无论行驶方向如何，驾驶员不得在布恩路（Boone Road）和百老汇路（Broadway）的交叉口向右转弯。
第二十六条. 驾驶员在与相反方向行驶的另一辆车交会时，应从左侧通过。
第二十七条. 当驾驶员与另一辆不同方向行驶的车辆同时到达没有交通执勤人员的交叉口时，应低速行驶，以便让另一辆车先行。驾驶员从小支路进入主干道时，应低速行驶，以便让其他车辆先行。无论前述规定如何，驾驶员应始终给予消防车或救护车服务车辆优先通行权。
第二十八条. 驾驶员在经过马匹或车辆时，如可行，应从右侧通过，此前需鸣笛、喊叫或使用其他形式的警告，使马匹或车辆让出通道供其通过，并等待第四十七条规定的信号。
第二十九条. 驾驶员在经过电车时，应从左侧通过，除非因道路状况导致无法这样做。

When Passing A Sentry

Article 32. No driver shall pass
another motor car or motorcycle go-
ing in the same direction, except a
bus; no driver of a truck shall pass
another truck going in the same
direction, on the following roads:—
North Szechuen Road, Woosung

In the vicinity of the crossing of

near to the kerb and stop to allow an

jured person or a funeral procession

Article 35. A driver of a motor
vehicle approaching a horse on a

winding place, or a crowded part of a

A pedestrian crossing.
Side of a tramcar standing on a

A slope or a bridge.
A sentry.
Article 38. No driver shall travel
abreast of another vehicle on a high-
way; he shall follow another vehicle
at less than 10m. space from the

Waiting Places

on highway in the same direction
and in one line as another vehicle at
a close distance shall follow the track
of the preceding vehicle and no driver
shall pass or attempt to pass another
vehicle at a crossing whether the

signal.
Article 40. No driver shall cause
a vehicle to remain at the entrance
to any premises in such a manner as
to obstruct access thereto longer than
is necessary for the expeditious taking
up or setting down of passengers, or
the loading or unloading of freight

Article 41. No driver shall back
his vehicle or turn it round in a
roadway if by so doing he obstructs
or endangers other traffic.
Article 42. A driver when stopping
or parking his vehicle in a roadway
for the purpose of taking up or
setting down of passengers or for any
other reason (except in obedience to

gendarme or a policeman) shall do

Article 43. No driver shall cause a
vehicle to wait or otherwise remain
stationary on the highway (except in
obedience to the instructions of a
sentry, gendarme or policeman) at

第三十条。驾驶员在驶过为上下乘客而停下的电车时，应低速行驶；如有必要，应停车直至道路畅通。当乘客正在上下车，或设有安全岛，或电车与其车辆之间有1.5米间距时，驾驶员可缓慢驶过电车。

第三十一条。除负责消防车或救护车服务的驾驶员外，任何驾驶员不得在街道交叉口、转弯或绕过弯道、下陡坡、驶过窄桥或前方视野不清时超越其他车辆。

经过哨兵时

第三十二条。除公共汽车外，任何驾驶员不得超越同向行驶的其他汽车或摩托车；在下列道路上，卡车驾驶员不得超越同向行驶的其他卡车：—
北四川路、吴淞路、乍浦路、昆山路、靶子路（Range Road）、海宁北路、
狄思威路与吉美路（Mahui Tohori）交叉口附近、西华德路（Nino Bashi以西）以及百老汇路（包括东百老汇路）。

第三十三条。当消防车或救护车从附近驶过时，所有驾驶员应靠近路边。

第三十四条。所有驾驶员应靠近路边并停车，以便载有病人或伤员的救护车或送葬队伍自由通行。

第三十五条。机动车驾驶员在公路上接近马匹时，如有必要或经要求，应减速或停车。

第三十六条。驾驶员在经过铁路道口时应停车，并确保通过是安全的，但若从警官、信号员或道路状况处获得此类保证，则可通过。

第三十七条。驾驶员在经过下列地点时应减速，并按喇叭、喊叫或发出信号：—
道路交叉口的弯道、曲折处或道路拥挤路段。
人行横道。
公路上无安全岛的电车侧面。
斜坡或桥梁。
哨兵。

第三十八条。任何驾驶员不得在公路上与其他车辆并排行驶；跟随前车时，与前车的间距应小于10米。

等候地点

第三十九条。驾驶员在公路上与另一车辆同向且近距离单列行驶时，应跟随前车的轨迹；无论后者是因警察信号而停止还是行驶，任何驾驶员均不得在交叉口超越或试图超越其他车辆。

第四十条。任何驾驶员不得使车辆停留在任何场所入口处以致阻碍进入，其停留时间不得超过迅速上下乘客或装卸货物所必需的时间。

第四十一条。如果倒车或掉头会阻碍或危及其他交通，任何驾驶员不得在车道上倒车或掉头。

第四十二条。驾驶员为上下乘客或其他原因（除非服从哨兵、宪兵或警察的指令）在车道上停车或停放车辆时，应将车辆左侧尽可能靠近左侧路缘石。

第四十三条。除服从哨兵、宪兵或警察的指令外，任何驾驶员不得在不允许的地点使车辆在公路上等候或以其他方式停留。

Article 44. Parking is prohibited at
the following places :—
Woosung Road (east side between

Article 45. A driver when leaving
his vehicle stationed or parked shall
do so after rendering the vehicle im-
movable and shall stop the motor if
it is practicable.

Article 46. No driver shall use a
horn, bell or other form of warning
signal unnecessarily beyond the re-
quirements of traffic safety.

Article 47. A driver when turning
or slowing down or stopping or al-
lowing other vehicles to pass by his
vehicle shall use the following signals,
except when he uses his signal ap-
paratus for turning and a lamp for
stopping :—
Stopping.—extend slightly downward
the right or left arm with clenched
fist out-side the vehicle.
Turning to the right.—extend the
right arm with fingers straightened
horizontally to the right from the
right side of the vehicle or raise left
arm with straightened fingers outside
the vehicle from the left.
Turning to the left.—extend the left
arm with fingers straightened hori-
zontally to the right from the right
side of the vehicle or raise right arm
with straightened fingers outside of
the vehicle from the right.
Go, pass.—extend the right arm with
straightened fingers from right side of
the vehicle wave it back and forth or
use left arm in the same way if use
of the right arm is impracticable.
Slow down.—extend right arm or left
arm with straightened fingers, down-
ward.
Go ahead.—extend the right or the
left arm, outside the vehicle toward
front making parallel line with the
traffic.

Article 48. No person shall stand
or sit on or otherwise occupy the
footboard of a vehicle in motion on
a highway.

Vehicles Barred

Article 49. No person shall drive a
motor vehicle on a highway who is
not in possession of any of the fol-
lowing licences :—
A licence issued by the Shanghai
Special Naval Landing Party or by the
Japanese army.
A licence issued by the S.M.C. or the
F.M.C.
A licence issued by the Japanese
Consulate-General or the "Reformed
Government."

Article 50. All drivers must always
carry their licence with them.

Article 51. No person shall drive
a vehicle on a highway when under
the influence of liquor or when smok-
ing.

Article 52. No person shall drive a
vehicle on a highway who is physi-
cally unfit to do so or who is suffer-
ing from mental disease.

Article 53. A driver when driving
a vehicle at night shall put on the
front head lights and the tail light
and when passing another vehicle
going in the opposite direction shall
reduce the power of the head lights
and turn downward the direction of
the lights so that no glare is emitted
that is necessary and put on the tail
lights.

禁止停车

第四十四条。下列地点禁止停车：—
吴淞路（海宁路与苏州河北路之间的东侧）；
乍浦路（海宁路与苏州河北路之间的东侧）；

第四十六条。除交通安全所需外，任何驾驶员不得无故使用喇叭、铃铛或其他形式的警告信号。

第四十七条。驾驶员在转弯、减速、停车或让其他车辆通过时，应使用下列信号，除非其使用转向信号装置和停车灯：—
停车。—将右臂或左臂稍向下伸出车外，握拳。
向右转弯。—从车辆右侧将右臂伸直，手指水平向右伸出；或从车辆左侧将左臂伸出车外，手指伸直举起。
向左转弯。—从车辆右侧将左臂伸直，手指水平向右伸出；或从车辆右侧将右臂伸出车外，手指伸直举起。
前行、通过。—从车辆右侧将右臂伸直，手指伸直，来回挥动；若使用右臂不可行，则以同样方式使用左臂。
减速。—将右臂或左臂伸直，手指向下。
向前行驶。—将右臂或左臂伸出车外指向前方，与交通流向平行。

第四十八条。任何人不得站立、坐于或以其他方式占据公路上行驶车辆的脚踏板。

禁止驾驶的车辆

第四十九条。未持有以下任何执照者，不得在公路上驾驶机动车辆：—
由上海特别海军陆战队或日本军队颁发的执照。
由工部局（S.M.C.）或公董局（F.M.C.）颁发的执照。
由日本总领事馆或“维新政府”颁发的执照。

第五十条。所有驾驶员必须随时携带执照。

第五十一条。任何人在受酒精影响或吸烟时，不得在公路上驾驶车辆。

第五十二条。身体不适合驾驶或患有精神疾病者，不得在公路上驾驶车辆。

第五十三条。驾驶员夜间驾驶车辆时应开启前大灯和尾灯；在与对向行驶的车辆交会时，应减弱前大灯亮度并将灯光方向朝下，以免产生必要的眩光，并开启尾灯。

distance of 50 m. ahead and a tail
light which enables a person to read
the licence plate at a distance of 25
m. from behind.
Vehicles which fail to exhibit clear-
ly any of the licence plates issued by
the Japanese Navy, the Japanese
Army, the Japanese Consulate-General,
the "Reformed Government," the
Shanghai Municipal Council or the
French Municipal Council.
Article 57. A driver when he has
injured a person or damaged a thing
shall stop the vehicle. In the first
case he shall take the necessary steps
to rescue the victim. Provided he
shall follow the instructions of the
sentry, gendarme or the police on the
scene.
The driver shall not continue on
his way until he has completely taken
the necessary steps mentioned above
and submitted a report to the mili-
tary police.
Or the police giving the number
of the vehicle, the names and
addresses of himself, employer and
the user of the vehicle and obtained
permission to leave; but in case there
is no gendarme or police on the scene
he shall without delay report the in-
cident to the gendarmerie and the
police.
A driver of a vehicle in the service
of the Fire Brigade, the Post Office,
an emergency motor car or an am-
bulance carrying an injured man or
a patient may continue on its way
after he has caused other men in
the service to take the prescribed
steps.
No passenger on the vehicle shall
obstruct the driver in taking the steps
mentioned in the above three para-
graphs.
Article 58. Whoever violates these
regulations will be prohibited to drive
a vehicle in the areas under the juris-
diction of the Shanghai Special Naval
Landing Party according to cir-
cumstances.

第五十四条。驾驶员经过哨兵线时应开启车厢内的灯光。

第五十五条。除拖拉机外，任何机动车辆不得拖曳其他车辆，除非发生事故需要普通车辆这样做。

第五十六条。车辆有下列六种缺陷之一时，不得在公路上行驶：—
动力控制系统、制动器、手柄、齿轮、变速齿轮存在机械故障。
车辆尺寸超过长7.5米、宽2.2米、高3米。
车辆所载货物尺寸超过高3.5米（小型车辆为1.8米）及长7.5米。
严重损坏路面、发出令公众厌烦的噪音、或产生大量令人反感的气味或有害气体或烟雾的车辆。
未配备能使驾驶员辨别前方50米处交通障碍物的前大灯，以及未配备能使后方25米处的人看清车牌的尾灯的车辆。
未能清晰展示由日本海军、日本陆军、日本总领事馆、“维新政府”、上海工部局或法国公董局颁发的任何车牌的车辆。

第五十七条。驾驶员致人受伤或损坏物品时应停车。在第一种情况下，他应采取必要措施救助受害者。但他应遵循现场哨兵、宪兵或警察的指令。
驾驶员在完成上述必要步骤并向宪兵队或警察提交报告，提供车辆号码、本人、雇主及车辆使用者的姓名和地址，并获得离开许可后，方可继续行驶；但若现场无宪兵或警察，他应立即向宪兵队和警察报告此事。
消防车、邮局、紧急机动车或载有伤员或病人的救护车的驾驶员，在安排其他服务人员采取规定措施后，可继续行驶。
车上乘客不得阻碍驾驶员采取上述三段所述的措施。

第五十八条。凡违反本条例者，将根据具体情况，被禁止在上海特别海军陆战队管辖区域内驾驶车辆。
